simulation_note.description: When conditioned on realistic random vectors z~N(0,I), the full softplus(Wz+b) output is highly variable (CV=118%, mean=1.54, p5=0.006, p95=5.36). The 0.75x suppression is the ZERO-CONDITIONING BASELINE. Under actual conditioning, the head produces a wide dynamic range — it is NOT uniformly suppressed at runtime. The bias term sets a ~0.755 floor, but the weight matrix (norm 15.57) allows large excursions.

verdict: CLAIM VERIFIED (with important caveat). All three quantitative sub-checks PASS against the raw bias vector: baseline mean=0.755 (within 0.012), CV=1.54% (well below 5%), weight norm=15.57 (exact match to claim). The claim is accurate for the BIAS BASELINE. The caveat is that the full conditioned output is NOT uniformly ~0.75: with random conditioning vectors the head produces scales ranging from near-zero to 11.7 (CV=118%). The '0.75x uniform suppression' characterizes only the intercept/prior of the learned function.
